issues.explanation: This node bundles five distinct named examples (projectile, collision, accelerating object, decelerating vehicle, heating water) into one node, violating the atomicity rule and the ~4-item chunk ceiling. Each example is independently testable.

new_nodes.label: Energy store changes for a projectile (kinetic to gravitational potential)
new_nodes.objective: Describe the energy store changes when an object is projected upwards.
essentialPoints: An object projected upwards: kinetic store transfers to gravitational potential store

new_nodes.label: Energy store changes in a collision (kinetic to thermal/sound)
new_nodes.objective: Describe the energy store changes when a moving object hits an obstacle.
essentialPoints: A moving object hitting an obstacle: kinetic store transfers to thermal/sound stores

new_nodes.label: Energy store changes for an object accelerated by a constant force
new_nodes.objective: Describe the energy store changes when an object is accelerated by a constant force.
essentialPoints: An object accelerated by a constant force: work done increases kinetic store

new_nodes.label: Energy store changes for a decelerating vehicle (kinetic to thermal)
new_nodes.objective: Describe the energy store changes when a vehicle slows down using brakes.
essentialPoints: A vehicle slowing down: kinetic store transfers to thermal store (brakes)

new_nodes.label: Energy store changes when heating water (e.g. in a kettle)
new_nodes.objective: Describe the energy store changes when water is heated by an electrical device.
essentialPoints: Heating water in a kettle: chemical/electrical transfer increases thermal store of water

issues.explanation: This node references dissipation as a rationale for comparing GPE lost vs KE gained but the removal of p1_energy_change_description leaves this dependent on the correct specific example node (braking/collision dissipation) rather than the bundled node.

This is an empty placeholder 'link' node with no objective/essentialPoints/specRefs content and duplicates the prerequisite relationship already expressed by the edge p1_system_def -> p1_energy_stores. It should be removed as it's not a genuine testable concept.

This is an empty placeholder node with objective 'placeholder' and no essentialPoints/specRefs, duplicating the existing edges from p6_transverse_wave and p6_longitudinal_wave to p6_wave_medium_evidence. Should be removed.

Malformed ID concatenating two other node ids; this is an evaluation node about choosing a radiation source but its id is confusing/non-standard and should be renamed for clarity and consistency (p4_ prefix convention should not embed two other ids).

new_nodes.label: Evaluating best radiation source for a given situation
new_nodes.objective: Apply knowledge of penetration, range and ionising power to evaluate the best type of radioactive source for a given use.
essentialPoints: Choice of source depends on required penetration/ionising power for the application
Must weigh benefits (e.g. penetration for imaging) against hazards (e.g. high ionising power near living tissue)

issues.explanation: Duplicate of p3_shc_definition (same label/objective/content: specific heat capacity definition) created independently in Topic 1 and Topic 3. Per the no-duplicate-id rule, these should be merged into one canonical node.

Duplicate of p3_shc_equation (same equation ΔE=mcΔθ) created independently in Topic 1 and Topic 3, and p1_rp1_procedure/p1_rp1_calculation duplicate p3_rp1_procedure/p3_rp1_calc_shc as the same RP1 practical. These parallel chains should be merged to avoid two disconnected copies of RP1.

This evaluation node about science's limits in resolving environmental issues from energy resource use is closely related to the general Topic 0 concept p0_power_limits_science (power and limitations of science) but has no edge to it, missing a genuine cross-topic prerequisite link.

The concept of efficiency (useful vs total energy/power) was already taught generically in Topic 1 (p1_efficiency_power_eq) but the National Grid efficiency explanation node in Topic 2 does not reference it, duplicating conceptual grounding instead of reusing the cross-topic prerequisite.

This node bundles three separate radiation types' penetration/range/ionising comparisons (alpha, beta, gamma) as one node's essentialPoints, each of which is independently testable and exceeds atomic single-idea granularity in effect (three named properties for three named particles).

new_nodes.label: Alpha radiation: penetration, range and ionising power
new_nodes.objective: Describe the penetrating power, range in air and ionising power of alpha radiation.
essentialPoints: Alpha: low penetration (stopped by paper/skin), short range in air, strongly ionising

new_nodes.label: Beta radiation: penetration, range and ionising power
new_nodes.objective: Describe the penetrating power, range in air and ionising power of beta radiation.
essentialPoints: Beta: medium penetration (stopped by ~few mm aluminium), medium range, moderately ionising

new_nodes.label: Gamma radiation: penetration, range and ionising power
new_nodes.objective: Describe the penetrating power, range in air and ionising power of gamma radiation.
essentialPoints: Gamma: highly penetrating (needs thick lead/concrete), long range, weakly ionising

This node duplicates p0_at1_measure_length_temp and p0_at1_mass_time_temp and p0_at1_length_mass_time_volume_temp (all cover using apparatus to measure length/mass/time/temperature). Multiple near-identical AT1 nodes were generated across different batches, violating the no-duplicate-id/concept rule and fragmenting prerequisite wiring for downstream practicals.

remainingProblems: Multiple near-duplicate AT1 apparatus-measurement nodes exist across Topic 0 (p0_at1_measure_length_temp, p0_at1_mass_time_temp, p0_at1_length_mass_time_volume_temp, p0_at1_length_mass_time, p0_at1_timer, p0_at1_micrometer_vernier, p0_at1_displacement_volume) and should ideally be consolidated into one canonical AT1 node family; only partial rewiring was performed here to avoid destabilizing the graph further.

Multiple near-duplicate WS/MS foundation nodes exist in Topic 0 under different ids/subtopics (e.g. p0_rearrange_equations vs p0_ms_rearrange vs p0_ms_rearrange_equations; p0_mean_range vs p0_ws_mean vs p0_ms_mean; p0_plot_graphs vs p0_ms_plot_graph vs p0_ms_graph_plotting vs p0_ms_graphs_gradient) representing the same underlying skills generated redundantly - a full consolidation pass is recommended but out of scope for this patch to preserve DAG stability.

p3_shc_definition and p3_shc_equation are retained as canonical versions after merging with the Topic 1 duplicates; downstream Topic 1 edges were repointed but a full audit of all p1_shc_* references elsewhere should be done.

The AT1 consolidation edge fix only repoints two example downstream edges (p5_rp7_procedure, p1_ws_gpe_ke_practical); other practical procedure nodes still reference the fragmented p0_at1_* variants and should be reviewed for consistency.
